Threat.value: When something takes longer than expected I assume something bad is happening
I jump or startle at ordinary sounds that would not bother most people
I feel threatened by strangers approaching me even in ordinary situations

Memory.value: Remembering the event brings back the same terror I felt at the time
My memories of the event feel more real and vivid than memories of ordinary things
The memory is so extreme it is hard to believe it actually happened to me

vignette: Sam, a 39-year-old male of Oceania descent, has been an airline pilot for over a decade. He recently divorced his wife and is now seeking help due to symptoms that have significantly disrupted his daily life and work. Sam's traumatic event occurred during a routine flight. On that fateful day, the plane he was piloting experienced mechanical issues, causing delays and unexpected stops. The situation escalated when local police officers arrived at the scene, creating an atmosphere of chaos and confusion. Sam vividly recalls the moment when the plane's engines started sputtering mid-flight, sending a wave of panic through him and his passengers. As they made an emergency landing, he felt the same terror that gripped him then whenever he thinks about the incident now. The memory feels so real and vivid to Sam that it's difficult for him to accept that this actually happened. He often finds himself questioning whether the event was more of a nightmare than reality. Since the trauma, Sam has experienced intense triggers in various aspects of his life. Physical proximity to others, especially when driving with colleagues or passengers, evokes feelings of unease and fear. The mere presence of other people during these moments brings back vivid recollections of that chaotic scene on the ground. He also experiences nausea whenever he thinks about being close to large groups or in confined spaces. These somatic reactions serve as potent reminders of his trauma. Sam's life has been marked by a heightened sense of threat, making him constantly vigilant and hypervigilant. Whenever something takes longer than expected, whether it's flight delays or routine procedures at work, he assumes the worst. This assumption leads to intense anxiety and an overwhelming belief that disaster is imminent. Ordinary sounds, like the hum of the airport tarmac or the chatter of passengers, now startle him, causing his heart to race and a cold sweat to break out. Sam also feels threatened by strangers approaching him in ordinary situations. While at work, he has become increasingly wary of interactions with ground staff, fearing that any unexpected encounter could lead to another traumatic incident. These feelings have led to significant avoidance behaviors. Sam has started avoiding social gatherings and flying routes where there is a high probability of encountering large crowds or delays. The consequences of these behaviors are evident in his work life. His hypervigilance and fear have made it difficult for him to engage with colleagues, leading to strained relationships and missed opportunities for collaboration. In one instance, he declined a leadership position on an important project because he feared the increased responsibility would lead to more stress and potential trauma triggers. Sam's personal life has also suffered. He has become distant from his family and friends, often citing work obligations as a reason but in reality, avoiding social interactions that might trigger his anxiety. His ex-wife reports feeling isolated by his withdrawal, which has further strained their relationship. What finally brought Sam to seek help was a recent incident where he almost caused an accident due to distraction during flight preparations. He realized then that his symptoms were not only affecting him but also putting the safety of others at risk. Despite his fears, Sam is most hopeful for regaining control over his life and finding ways to cope with his traumatic memories without letting them dictate his actions. In therapy, he expresses a deep-seated fear that another traumatic event will occur, leaving him feeling powerless. He hopes to learn strategies to manage his anxiety and develop healthier coping mechanisms to handle the vivid and terrifying memories of that day on the flight. Sam's journey towards recovery is marked by a willingness to confront his fears and find new ways to navigate through his daily life as an airline pilot without being overwhelmed by the past trauma.
